items.name: Numerical Picard local system
items.statement: For a proper scheme X over a field k, Pic^τ_{X/k} is the open subgroup of geometrically numerically trivial line bundles and Num_{X/k}=Pic_{X/k}/Pic^τ_{X/k}; it is an étale local system with geometric fiber a finite-rank free abelian group.

tests.name: NumericalPicardlocalsystemTest1
tests.statement: Num(P¹_k)=Z via degree.

tests.name: NumericalPicardlocalsystemTest2
tests.statement: Numerically trivial bundles map to zero, including torsion bundles.

tests.name: NumericalPicardlocalsystemTest3
tests.statement: For P¹_C viewed over R, geometric Num is Z² with nontrivial conjugation; it is not constant.

items.name: Positive-power descent criterion
items.statement: For proper X/k, Num_{X/k} is constant iff some positive integer d has this property: for every line bundle L on X_kalg there exists a numerically trivial line bundle N on X_kalg such that L^⊗d⊗N descends to X.
items.note: Use d≥1; printed d≥0 admits the vacuous value zero. Arbitrary proper X, not only geometrically connected X.

items.name: Component dual graph
items.statement: For a noetherian scheme X, Γ(X) has its irreducible components as vertices, with an edge between distinct components iff their intersection is nonempty.

tests.name: ComponentdualgraphTest1
tests.statement: An integral curve has one vertex.

tests.name: ComponentdualgraphTest2
tests.statement: Two components meeting at two points still give one adjacency edge in this convention.

tests.name: ComponentdualgraphTest3
tests.statement: A disconnected union of two curves has no edge.

items.name: Curve criterion for numerical constancy
items.statement: For a proper one-dimensional k-scheme X and geometric point Spec Ω→Spec k, Num_{X/k} is constant iff Γ(X_Ω)→Γ(X) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Contraction
items.statement: A contraction of proper schemes is a proper morphism f:X→Y for which O_Y→f_*O_X is an isomorphism.

tests.name: ContractionTest1
tests.statement: The identity is a contraction.

tests.name: ContractionTest2
tests.statement: A connected-fiber morphism with Stein factor O_Y is a contraction.

tests.name: ContractionTest3
tests.statement: A disconnected finite étale cover of degree two is not a contraction.

items.name: Descent of geometric contractions
items.statement: Let X/k be proper with constant Num_{X/k}. Every contraction X_{kalg}→Y with projective target descends to a contraction X→Y₀ over k.
items.note: The target's projectivity is a hypothesis; descent includes its identification after base change.

items.name: Purely inseparable contraction descent
items.statement: For a purely inseparable field extension k⊂k′, every contraction of X_{k′}, with X proper over k, descends to k; this branch does not require constant Num or projectivity of the target.

items.name: Torsion in the Picard descent obstruction
items.statement: For proper h:X→Spec k, H²(Spec k,h_*G_m) is torsion.
items.note: Proof reduces via the finite Artin affinization algebra, its nilpotent filtration, and field Brauer groups.

items.name: Intersection-labelled component graph
items.statement: For a proper curve on a smooth proper surface S/k with H⁰(S,O)=k, attach to each pair of distinct components their surface intersection number as an edge label.

tests.name: IntersectionlabelledcomponentgraphTest1
tests.statement: Transverse rational components meeting once have label 1.

tests.name: IntersectionlabelledcomponentgraphTest2
tests.statement: Two components meeting transversely twice have label 2.

tests.name: IntersectionlabelledcomponentgraphTest3
tests.statement: The unlabelled graph alone cannot distinguish labels 1 and 2.

items.name: Fiber graph descent
items.statement: Let f:S→Z be a contraction of a smooth proper k-surface with H⁰(O_S)=k. Let ā:Spec Ω→Z have image a, with Ω algebraically closed, and suppose S_ā is one-dimensional. If Num_{S/k} is constant, Γ(S_ā)→Γ(S_a) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Descent of fiber intersection labels
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, if (S_a)_red is geometrically reduced, that graph isomorphism also preserves edge labels.

items.name: Residue field of a reducible geometric fiber
items.statement: Under Theorem 2.1, if S_ā is reducible, the field extension k⊂κ(a) is purely inseparable.

items.name: Curves of fiber and canonical type
items.statement: On a smooth proper surface, a connected effective divisor C=Σm_iC_i is of fiber type if C·C_i=0 for every i; it is indecomposable if gcd_i m_i=1, and of canonical type if also K·C_i=0.

tests.name: CurvesoffiberandcanonicaltypeTest1
tests.statement: A smooth genus-one fiber has multiplicity 1.

tests.name: CurvesoffiberandcanonicaltypeTest2
tests.statement: Twice an indecomposable fiber has multiplicity 2 and the same underlying divisor.

tests.name: CurvesoffiberandcanonicaltypeTest3
tests.statement: A negative-definite exceptional divisor is not of fiber type.

items.name: Rationality of singular-fiber components over finite fields
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a genus-one fibration on a smooth proper F_q-surface with H⁰(O_S)=F_q and constant Num. Assume the underlying geometric fiber at a is singular. Then geometric reducibility implies a is rational, and a is rational iff all components of S_a are birational over F_q to P¹.
items.note: Added singularity restriction: the displayed equivalence in the preprint is false for a smooth elliptic fiber. The graph-descent assertion itself has no such restriction.

items.name: Split semistable fiber count
items.statement: For a genus-one fibration on a smooth proper F_q-surface with constant Num, a fiber over a rational point whose reduced curve is singular, has r components and type split I_r has r q rational points. Multiplicities do not change this count.

items.name: Nonsplit nodal fiber count
items.statement: For a genus-one fibration on a smooth proper F_q-surface with constant Num, a fiber over a rational point whose reduced curve is singular, has r components and type nonsplit I₁ has q+2 rational points. Multiplicities do not change this count.

items.name: Nonsplit two-component fiber count
items.statement: For a genus-one fibration on a smooth proper F_q-surface with constant Num, a fiber over a rational point whose reduced curve is singular, has r components and type nonsplit I₂ has 2q+2 rational points. Multiplicities do not change this count.

items.name: Additive fiber count
items.statement: For a genus-one fibration on a smooth proper F_q-surface with constant Num, a fiber over a rational point whose reduced curve is singular, has r components and type unstable has r q+1 rational points. Multiplicities do not change this count.

items.name: No I₀* fiber over F₂ with constant numerical Picard
items.statement: Such a fibration over F₂ has no I₀* fiber: its central rational component would contain four distinct rational intersection points, whereas P¹(F₂) has three points.

items.name: Elliptic curve E1 over F₂
items.statement: The smooth projective Weierstrass curve y²+y=x³+x²+1 over F₂ has cyclic rational-point group of order 1, j=0, and is supersingular.
acceptance: Explicitly enumerate the F₂ affine points and include the point at infinity.

items.name: Elliptic curve E2 over F₂
items.statement: The smooth projective Weierstrass curve y²+xy=x³+x²+x over F₂ has cyclic rational-point group of order 2, j=1, and is ordinary.
acceptance: Explicitly enumerate the F₂ affine points and include the point at infinity.

items.name: Elliptic curve E3 over F₂
items.statement: The smooth projective Weierstrass curve y²+y=x³ over F₂ has cyclic rational-point group of order 3, j=0, and is supersingular.
acceptance: Explicitly enumerate the F₂ affine points and include the point at infinity.

items.name: Elliptic curve E4 over F₂
items.statement: The smooth projective Weierstrass curve y²+xy=x³+x over F₂ has cyclic rational-point group of order 4, j=1, and is ordinary.
acceptance: Explicitly enumerate the F₂ affine points and include the point at infinity.

items.name: Elliptic curve E5 over F₂
items.statement: The smooth projective Weierstrass curve y²+y=x³+x² over F₂ has cyclic rational-point group of order 5, j=0, and is supersingular.
acceptance: Explicitly enumerate the F₂ affine points and include the point at infinity.

items.name: Five elliptic isomorphism classes over F₂
items.statement: Every elliptic curve over F₂ is isomorphic over F₂ to exactly one of E₁,…,E₅ of Proposition 3.3; its number of F₂-points determines the class.
items.note: Finite Weierstrass-coordinate enumeration independently checked; this does not classify genus-one fibrations.

items.name: Enriques surface
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k, an Enriques surface is a smooth proper k-surface Y with H⁰(O_Y)=k, numerically trivial canonical class, and ℓ-adic b₂=10 (ℓ≠char k). Over other fields use this geometric condition.

tests.name: EnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: A characteristic-two classical Enriques surface has nontrivial canonical bundle of order 2.

tests.name: EnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The numerical condition is weaker than requiring the canonical bundle to be trivial.

tests.name: EnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: A K3 surface, with b₂=22, is not Enriques.

items.name: Numerically trivial Picard group of an Enriques surface
items.statement: For an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field, Pic^τ is finite of length 2 and its k-points are generated by ω_Y.

items.name: Enriques numerical and cohomological invariants
items.statement: For such Y, Num(Y) is free of rank 10, b₁=b₃=0, b₂=ρ=10, and h¹(O_Y)=h²(O_Y)≤1.

items.name: Enriques numerical lattice
items.statement: The intersection form on Num(Y) is even unimodular of signature(1,9), and Num(Y)≅U⊕E₈(-1), where U has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,0]].
items.note: The geometric identification is missing; the abstract E₈ and integral-lattice APIs are already built and imported.

items.name: Existence of genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Every Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field admits a genus-one fibration to P¹.

items.name: Double fibers
items.statement: Every genus-one fibration on such an Enriques surface has a multiple fiber, and every multiple fiber has multiplicity 2.

items.name: Integral two-sections
items.statement: Every genus-one fibration on such a surface has an integral two-section, which can be chosen as either a (-2)-curve or a half-fiber of another genus-one fibration.
items.note: Never replace an integral two-section by a (-2)-curve without proof.

items.name: Half-fiber
items.statement: A half-fiber F of a genus-one fibration on an Enriques surface is the effective divisor with 2F equal to a fiber over a rational base point.
api: fiber class equals twice half-fiber class
uniqueness from its effective line bundle

tests.name: HalffiberTest1
tests.statement: F²=0.

tests.name: HalffiberTest2
tests.statement: A two-section C has C·F=1.

tests.name: HalffiberTest3
tests.statement: The reduced support of a reducible double fiber need not equal its half-fiber divisor.

items.name: Classical Enriques criteria
items.statement: For an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field, these are equivalent: ω_Y has order 2; H¹(O_Y)=0; some genus-one fibration has no wild fibers; some genus-one fibration has two multiple fibers.

items.name: Tame double fibers and canonical bundle
items.statement: Under those equivalent conditions every genus-one fibration has exactly two tame double fibers 2F₁,2F₂, with ω_Y≅O_Y(F₁−F₂); the conditions always hold if char k≠2.

items.name: Characteristic-two tame half-fiber types
items.statement: If char k=2 and a genus-one fibration on an Enriques surface has two distinct double fibers 2F₁,2F₂, each F_i is ordinary elliptic or unstable; neither is supersingular elliptic or semistable.

items.name: ordinary Enriques surface
items.statement: In characteristic 2 an Enriques surface is ordinary iff Pic^τ=μ₂; its Cartier-dual canonical-cover group is Z/2, its étale fundamental group is Z/2, and its canonical bundle is trivial.
api: type under algebraically closed field extension

tests.name: ordinaryEnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: The Picard group scheme for this type is μ₂.

tests.name: ordinaryEnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The cover group is the Cartier dual Z/2, not Pic^τ itself.

tests.name: ordinaryEnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: The type is disjoint from the other two characteristic-two types.

items.name: classical Enriques surface
items.statement: In characteristic 2 an Enriques surface is classical iff Pic^τ=Z/2; its Cartier-dual canonical-cover group is μ₂, its étale fundamental group is trivial, and its canonical bundle is order 2.
api: type under algebraically closed field extension

tests.name: classicalEnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: The Picard group scheme for this type is Z/2.

tests.name: classicalEnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The cover group is the Cartier dual μ₂, not Pic^τ itself.

tests.name: classicalEnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: The type is disjoint from the other two characteristic-two types.

items.name: supersingular Enriques surface
items.statement: In characteristic 2 an Enriques surface is supersingular iff Pic^τ=α₂; its Cartier-dual canonical-cover group is α₂, its étale fundamental group is trivial, and its canonical bundle is trivial.
api: type under algebraically closed field extension

tests.name: supersingularEnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: The Picard group scheme for this type is α₂.

tests.name: supersingularEnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The cover group is the Cartier dual α₂, not Pic^τ itself.

tests.name: supersingularEnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: The type is disjoint from the other two characteristic-two types.

items.name: K3-like canonical covering
items.statement: For a simply connected Enriques surface in characteristic 2 (classical or supersingular), the inclusion Pic^τ→Pic determines a nontrivial torsor X→Y for its local Cartier dual; this universal homeomorphism is called its K3-like covering.

tests.name: KlikecanonicalcoveringTest1
tests.statement: The cover has degree 2.

tests.name: KlikecanonicalcoveringTest2
tests.statement: Its total space is integral and Cohen–Macaulay with ω_X trivial.

tests.name: KlikecanonicalcoveringTest3
tests.statement: The total space is singular, so K3-like does not mean a smooth K3 surface.

items.name: Cohomology of the K3-like cover
items.statement: For the preceding canonical cover, h⁰(O_X)=h²(O_X)=1 and h¹(O_X)=0, and its singular locus is nonempty.

items.name: Conductrix and exceptionality
items.statement: For a simply connected characteristic-two Enriques surface, let X′ be the normalization of its K3-like cover. The map X′→Y is finite flat purely inseparable of degree 2. The ramification divisor R′ for X′→X is pulled back from an effective Cartier divisor C on Y, the conductrix; 2C is the biconductrix. Y is exceptional iff h¹(O_{2C})≠0.

tests.name: ConductrixandexceptionalityTest1
tests.statement: If C=0 then h¹(O_{2C})=0.

tests.name: ConductrixandexceptionalityTest2
tests.statement: The biconductrix is twice C as a divisor.

tests.name: ConductrixandexceptionalityTest3
tests.statement: Simply connected alone does not imply exceptional.

items.name: Nonexceptional quasielliptic restriction
items.statement: On a nonexceptional Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, no quasielliptic fibration has a simple III* or II* fiber.

items.name: Nonexceptional multiple exceptional-type restriction
items.statement: On such a surface, no genus-one fibration with a multiple IV*, III*, or II* fiber admits a (-2)-curve two-section.

items.name: Partner genus-one fibration
items.statement: For every genus-one fibration on a nonexceptional Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, another genus-one fibration has fiber-class intersection 4 with it.

items.name: Family of Enriques surfaces
items.statement: Over a ring R, an Enriques family is a flat proper finitely presented algebraic space Y→Spec R whose geometric fibers are Enriques surfaces. Isomorphisms and base change give the fppf stack M_Enr over affine Z-schemes.

tests.name: FamilyofEnriquessurfacesTest1
tests.statement: A family pulls back to every R-algebra.

tests.name: FamilyofEnriquessurfacesTest2
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field this recovers the surface definition.

tests.name: FamilyofEnriquessurfacesTest3
tests.statement: Restricting the definition to schemes would lose the stated algebraic-space scope.

items.name: No Enriques surface over the integers
items.statement: There is no Enriques family over Z; equivalently M_Enr(Z) is empty.
items.note: Depends on the repaired Proposition 5.5 chain /63, Fontaine /147–/148, the exceptional lifting input /48, and the full finite-field endpoint /146. Recursive source closure remains partial.

items.name: Exceptional fibers do not lift modulo four
items.statement: There is no Enriques family over Z/4Z whose geometric special fiber is exceptional.

items.name: Relative Picard representability
items.statement: For an Enriques family over any ring R, its fppf relative Picard algebraic space is a scheme.

items.name: Relative numerical invariants
items.statement: For such a family, Pic^τ is an open subgroup locally free of rank 2 and Num is an étale local system of free abelian groups of rank 10.

items.name: Rank-two Oort–Tate group
items.statement: For an invertible R-module L and a∈L,b∈L^(-1) with a⊗b=2, define G(A)={f∈L⊗A:f²=a f}, with operation f⋆g=f+g−bfg.

tests.name: RanktwoOortTategroupTest1
tests.statement: (L,a,b)=(R,1, 2) gives the constant group Z/2.

tests.name: RanktwoOortTategroupTest2
tests.statement: (R,2, 1) gives μ₂ via u=1−f.

tests.name: RanktwoOortTategroupTest3
tests.statement: The plus sign fails over Z at a=1,b=2,f=g=1:4 is not idempotent.

items.name: Classification of finite flat groups of rank two
items.statement: Every finite locally free group scheme of rank 2 over a ring R is isomorphic to the group associated with an invertible module and a⊗b=2 as above.
items.note: Introduction and exact rank-two contract read; full classification proof not yet extracted.

items.name: Rank-two Cartier duality
items.statement: The Cartier dual of the group associated with (L,a,b) is associated with (L^(-1),b,a).

items.name: Rank-two groups over Z
items.statement: Over Z every finite flat rank-two group is isomorphic to Z/2 or μ₂.

items.name: Family of canonical coverings
items.statement: For an Enriques family f:Y→S, set P=Pic^τ_{Y/S}, G=P^D. The inclusion P→Pic gives [X]∈H⁰(S,R¹f_*G_Y); a canonical covering family is a G_Y-torsor whose cohomology class maps to [X].

tests.name: FamilyofcanonicalcoveringsTest1
tests.statement: A section of f kills the obstruction.

tests.name: FamilyofcanonicalcoveringsTest2
tests.statement: Two covers differ by a pulled-back G-torsor from S.

tests.name: FamilyofcanonicalcoveringsTest3
tests.statement: Existence of a local cover alone does not identify it with a chosen global cover.

items.name: Canonical-cover obstruction
items.statement: For an Enriques family the exact sequence 0→H¹(S,G)→H¹(Y,G_Y)→H⁰(S,R¹f_*G_Y)→H²(S,G)→H²(Y,G_Y) makes the image of [X] the obstruction to a canonical cover.

items.name: Injective pullback criterion for a canonical cover
items.statement: For an Enriques family over S=Spec R with P=Pic^τ and G=P^D, a canonical-cover family exists if H²(S,G)→H²(Y,G_Y) is injective.

items.name: Section criterion for a canonical cover
items.statement: For an Enriques family over S=Spec R with P=Pic^τ and G=P^D, a canonical-cover family exists if f admits a section.

items.name: Étale Picard torsion criterion for a canonical cover
items.statement: For an Enriques family over S=Spec R with P=Pic^τ and G=P^D, a canonical-cover family exists if P→S is étale and Pic(S)=0.

items.name: Twisting of canonical coverings
items.statement: When a canonical-cover family exists, its isomorphism classes form a torsor under H¹(S,G), acting by pullback and twisting.

items.name: Constant and split Picard schemes
items.statement: For an Enriques family, constant Num means Num≅Z¹⁰_S; constant Picard means Pic≅(Z/2×Z¹⁰)_S. Split Picard means the extension 0→Pic^τ→Pic→Num→0 splits.
api: splitting by lifts of a numerical basis

tests.name: ConstantandsplitPicardschemesTest1
tests.statement: Constant full Picard implies constant Num.

tests.name: ConstantandsplitPicardschemesTest2
tests.statement: An extension by Z/2 splits if every basis element lifts to a section.

tests.name: ConstantandsplitPicardschemesTest3
tests.statement: Constant Num alone does not force Pic^τ to be the constant Z/2 group.

items.name: Constant Picard scheme over Z
items.statement: Every Enriques family over Z has constant full Picard scheme.
items.note: Use /63’s four-twist repair and local scheme models before invoking Fontaine. Num constancy is established first from /180–/181; it does not depend on /62. Once μ₂ is excluded, finite étale Z/2-torsors above each numerical basis vector split over Z.

items.name: Canonical-cover compatibility at two
items.statement: If Y/Z is an Enriques family with Pic^τ=μ₂, then for any canonical double cover X of Y over Z[1/2], one of its twists by 1,−1,2,−2 has a generic K3 fiber admitting a smooth proper projective scheme model over Z_p for every prime p. In particular it has the required good reduction over W(F₂bar) at 2.
items.note: Previously unverified comparison now has an explicit mathematical proof in the report, assembled from /172–/188 and /54–/60,/79–/80. Choose a Z₂-cover first, correct its Q₂-difference by the globally supported twist, and extend the residual unramified class 5. The proof is proposed for independent review, not a Lean verification. Arbitrary global and local covers need not coincide.

items.name: Canonical covers with constant Picard
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Canonical-cover families exist, and their isomorphism classes form a torsor under R×/(R×)².

items.name: Canonical bundle order
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. ω_{Y_k} has order 2 in Pic(Y_k).

items.name: Descent of numerical classes
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Each geometric numerical class comes from a line bundle on Y_k, uniquely up to tensoring by ω_{Y_k}.

items.name: Descent of (-2)-curves
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Every (-2)-curve on Y_kbar descends to a (-2)-curve on Y_k isomorphic to P¹_k.

items.name: Descent of genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Every genus-one fibration Y_kbar→P¹_kbar descends to Y_k→P¹_k.

items.name: Rational tame double fibers
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Every descended genus-one fibration has exactly two multiple fibers, both tame, over k-rational base points.

items.name: Existence over the residue field
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Y_k has at least one genus-one fibration to P¹_k.

items.name: Rational Jacobian Weierstrass model
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. Contract all vertical curves disjoint from E to the normal Weierstrass model Z; over k[t] its equation is y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆, with deg a_i≤i; over k[t⁻¹] use a′_i=a_i/t^i.

tests.name: RationalJacobianWeierstrassmodelTest1
tests.statement: The coefficient a₆ transforms by t⁻⁶.

tests.name: RationalJacobianWeierstrassmodelTest2
tests.statement: A reducible fiber can be contracted on Z even though J is smooth.

tests.name: RationalJacobianWeierstrassmodelTest3
tests.statement: O_J(3E) is not relatively very ample on a vertical component disjoint from E; the embedding concerns Z.

items.name: Canonical sheaf and zero-section on a rational Jacobian
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. ω_J=φ*O(-1), E²=−1, and ω_{J/P¹}=φ*O(1).

items.name: Weierstrass pushforward splitting
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. φ_*O_J(3E)≅O⊕O(-2)⊕O(-3); the relative Proj construction gives the cubic equation of the Weierstrass model.

items.name: Nonconstant rational-surface coefficients
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. In such a degree-bounded Weierstrass equation some a_i is nonconstant and some a_i is not divisible by t^i; these conditions survive degree-preserving admissible coordinate changes.
items.note: Source statement retained; minimality/rationality hypotheses are essential.

items.name: Jacobian of an Enriques genus-one fibration
items.statement: For an Enriques surface Y/k and genus-one fibration with generic fiber Y_η over K=k(t), use Pic⁰_{Y_η/K} in the elliptic case, and its unique regular compactification in the quasielliptic case; its relatively minimal regular surface model J→P¹ is the Jacobian fibration with zero-section.

tests.name: JacobianofanEnriquesgenusonefibrationTest1
tests.statement: The elliptic generic Jacobian is an elliptic curve.

tests.name: JacobianofanEnriquesgenusonefibrationTest2
tests.statement: The quasielliptic Pic⁰ is a form of G_a and needs compactification.

tests.name: JacobianofanEnriquesgenusonefibrationTest3
tests.statement: One must not treat a quasielliptic generic fiber as a smooth elliptic curve.

items.name: Rationality of the Enriques Jacobian
items.statement: The regular Jacobian surface of a genus-one fibration on an Enriques surface over any field is geometrically rational.

items.name: Algebraic-cycle zeta formula
items.statement: Let X/F_q be smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=F_q, and ℓ≠char F_q. If H^{2j+1}(Xbar,Q_ℓ)=0 for every j≥0 and the BASE-FIELD cycle map CH^j(X)⊗Q_ℓ→H^{2j}(Xbar,Q_ℓ(j)) is surjective for every j≥0, then Z(X,T)=∏_j(1−q^jT)^(−b_{2j}).
items.note: Cycles on Xbar alone do not imply trivial Frobenius on the twisted group.

items.name: Algebraic-cycle point-count formula
items.statement: Let X/F_q be smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=F_q, and ℓ≠char F_q. Under the preceding odd-vanishing and base-defined-cycle-surjectivity hypotheses, #X(F_{q^r})=Σ_j b_{2j}q^{jr} for every r≥1.
items.note: The r=1 formula is displayed; r≥1 follows by retaining the same Frobenius eigenvalues.

items.name: Surface count from constant Num
items.statement: Let X/F_q be smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=F_q, and ℓ≠char F_q. If X is a surface with b₁=0, b₂=ρ and constant Num_{X/F_q}, then #X(F_q)=1+b₂q+q².
items.note: Correct the printed F_p to F_q; b₃=0 follows by duality.

items.name: Twenty-five points over F₂
items.statement: An Enriques surface, or a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal genus-one surface, over F₂ with constant Num has exactly 25 F₂-points.

items.name: Isogeny for multiple fibers
items.statement: Let R be an excellent DVR with fraction field F and residue field k, let E/R be an elliptic scheme, and let X/R be the relatively minimal regular model of a torsor under E_F whose reduced special fiber is an elliptic curve. The elliptic curves E_k and (X_k)_red are isogenous over k.

items.name: Multiple-fiber extension counts
items.statement: Let R be an excellent DVR with fraction field F and residue field k, let E/R be an elliptic scheme, and let X/R be the relatively minimal regular model of a torsor under E_F whose reduced special fiber is an elliptic curve. If k=F_q, then #E_k(F_{q^r})=#X_k(F_{q^r}) for every r≥1.

items.name: Multiple-fiber isomorphism over F₂
items.statement: Let R be an excellent DVR with fraction field F and residue field k, let E/R be an elliptic scheme, and let X/R be the relatively minimal regular model of a torsor under E_F whose reduced special fiber is an elliptic curve. If k=F₂, then E_k≅(X_k)_red over F₂.

items.name: Genus under domination of an elliptic curve
items.statement: For any field k, an integral proper k-curve C with a dominant morphism to an elliptic curve E/k satisfies h¹(O_C)≥1.

items.name: Regularity in the genus-one equality case
items.statement: In the preceding situation, h¹(O_C)=1 implies that C is regular.
items.note: Do not strengthen regular to smooth over an imperfect field without proof.

items.name: Quotient models of multiple fibers
items.statement: Let R contain a residue-field representative k, let A/k be an abelian variety, G⊂A(k) a finite subgroup, and F′/Frac R a G-Galois extension whose integral closure R′ has the same residue field k. The free diagonal action gives X=(A×Spec R′)/G, with generic fiber a form of A and reduced special fiber A/G.

tests.name: QuotientmodelsofmultiplefibersTest1
tests.statement: For G=0 the model is A_R.

tests.name: QuotientmodelsofmultiplefibersTest2
tests.statement: The reduced special fiber is the quotient by translations.

tests.name: QuotientmodelsofmultiplefibersTest3
tests.statement: The multiple fiber must not be identified with its reduction as a scheme.

items.name: Constant Picard of the Jacobian
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. J has constant Picard scheme.

items.name: Matching geometric Kodaira types
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. At every geometric point over a closed point a∈P¹, the underlying indecomposable fibers of Y and J have the same Kodaira symbol.
items.note: Use Liu–Lorenzini–Raynaud 6.6 after passage to algebraically closed residue field, keeping multiplicity separate.

items.name: Simple-fiber identification
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. If Y_a is simple, J_a≅Y_a over κ(a).
items.note: For the smooth-locus point in Proposition 9.2, distinguish tree-shaped additive fibers (choose a multiplicity-one terminal component) from I_n cycles. A cycle has no terminal component; choose any component and remove its at most two intersection points. Over F₂ a rational P¹ still has a smooth point. Nonsplit I₁/I₂ use their conductor descriptions. This is a proof clarification, not a new fiber-isomorphism assertion.

items.name: Nonrational fibers
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. Every geometric fiber of J over a non-F₂-rational closed point of P¹ is irreducible.

items.name: Excluded I₀*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. No geometric fiber of J is of type I₀*.

items.name: Semistable graph descent
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. For every semistable geometric fiber, Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) is an isomorphism.

items.name: At most one semistable or supersingular rational fiber
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. At most one a∈P¹(F₂) has J_a semistable or smooth supersingular.

items.name: Descent of all Mordell–Weil sections
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. MW(J/P¹)=MW(Jbar/P¹bar).
items.note: The printed Br(F₂(t))=0 is false. Proposed repair uses Tsen over F₂bar(t) and the Galois-equivariant quotient of geometric Picard; see report.

items.name: Fiber-count input for Picard descent
items.statement: For a rational Jacobian elliptic surface over F₂ and a rational base point a, let r_a be its geometric component count. Put n_a=i for smooth E_i, 2r_a for split semistable, 2r_a+2 for nonsplit semistable, and 2r_a+1 for unstable fiber. This is a formal input until splitting is proved.
api: sum over three rational base points

tests.name: FibercountinputforPicarddescentTest1
tests.statement: For a split I₄ fiber n_a=8.

tests.name: FibercountinputforPicarddescentTest2
tests.statement: For a nonsplit I₂ fiber n_a=6.

tests.name: FibercountinputforPicarddescentTest3
tests.statement: Before graph descent, n_a is not automatically the actual point count of J_a.

items.name: Picard constancy criterion for rational elliptic surfaces
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹. Assume every nonrational geometric fiber is irreducible, no fiber is I₀*, every semistable fiber has split component graph, at most one rational fiber is semistable or supersingular, and every geometric Mordell–Weil section descends to F₂. If Σ_{a∈P¹(F₂)}n_a=25 with n_a defined above, then Pic_{J/F₂} is constant.

items.name: Additive graph rigidity
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹. Assume every nonrational geometric fiber is irreducible, no fiber is I₀*, every semistable fiber has split component graph, at most one rational fiber is semistable or supersingular, and every geometric Mordell–Weil section descends to F₂. If additionally Σn_a=25, then for every rational a with singular J_a the map Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) is an isomorphism.
items.note: The claim in the proof that orthogonal projection preserves the pairing is not used. Report supplies a dual-lattice argument requiring review.

items.name: Even unimodular complement for a rational Jacobian
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. Over an algebraic closure, the orthogonal complement W of the fiber F and zero-section O in Num(Jbar) is even unimodular of rank 8; it is generated by vertical components disjoint from O and (P−O)−(1+P·O)F for sections P.
items.note: The span of F,O has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,-1]]; the geometric statement is not supplied by abstract lattice APIs.

items.name: Geometric torsor Kodaira comparison
items.statement: Let R be a DVR with algebraically closed residue field, C/K a smooth geometrically connected genus-one curve of period m, E/K its Jacobian, and X,E_min their proper regular minimal models. If E_min has Kodaira type T, then X has type mT.
items.note: Statement and proof read. Do not apply without algebraically closed residue field: their Remark 6.8 warns it fails more generally. The 2018 corrigendum corrects §4 Brauer formulas, not the statement of 6.6.

items.name: Existence of a large rational fiber
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. Some rational fiber has at least six irreducible components.
acceptance: Assuming every component count≤5 gives at most 10+7+7=24 points, contrary to 25.

items.name: Existence of a reducible additive fiber
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. There is a reducible unstable fiber over a rational base point.

items.name: Unique additive fiber for nonzero functional j
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. If j∈F₂(t) is nonzero, exactly one fiber is unstable.
items.note: The intermediate c₄ criterion needs Δ=0; a smooth supersingular fiber is not additive.

items.name: Small additive fiber configuration
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. If j≠0 and the unique unstable fiber has at most five components, the rational-fiber configuration, up to a base automorphism, is III+E₄+I₈.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 1
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy+t²y=x³+tx²+t⁴x+t⁵(1+t) has functional j=t⁴, discriminant t⁸ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types I₁*+E₄+I₄.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 2
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy=x³+t³x+t⁵(1+t) has functional j=t²/(t²+t+1), discriminant t¹⁰(t²+t+1) on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types III*+E₄+E₄.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 3
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy=x³+t³x has functional j=t², discriminant t¹⁰ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types III*+E₄+I₂.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 4
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy=x³+t²x²+t³x has functional j=t², discriminant t¹⁰ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types III*+E₂+nonsplit I₂.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 5
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy=x³+t⁵ has functional j=t, discriminant t¹¹ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types II*+E₄+I₁.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 6
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy=x³+t²x²+t⁵ has functional j=t, discriminant t¹¹ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types II*+E₂+nonsplit I₁.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 7
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy=x³+tx²+t⁴x has functional j=1, discriminant t¹² on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types I₄*+E₂+E₄.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 8
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy+ty=x³+tx²+tx has functional j=t⁸, discriminant t⁴ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types III+E₄+I₈.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 9
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+t²y=x³+tx² has functional j=0, discriminant t⁸ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types I₁*+E₅+IV.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 10
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+t²y=x³+t³x has functional j=0, discriminant t⁸ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types IV*+E₅+III.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 11
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+t²y=x³ has functional j=0, discriminant t⁸ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types IV*+E₃+IV.
items.note: The exact regression checks the equation's invariants and smooth fiber at 1, not the minimal resolution or its Kodaira type.

items.name: Classification with nonzero functional j
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. If j≠0, exactly one of the eight models in Theorem 10.4 represents the fibration up to admissible Weierstrass coordinate changes and automorphisms of P¹.
items.note: Full Lang 2000 classification proof not acquired; finite invariant checks do not establish exhaustiveness.

items.name: Nonrational fibers of the eight nonzero-j models
items.statement: For the eight models of Theorem 10.4, all fibers at nonrational base points are smooth except in the j=t²/(t²+t+1) model, which has an I₁ fiber at the unique degree-two point t²+t+1=0.

items.name: Classification with zero functional j
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. If j=0, exactly one of the three models in Theorem 10.5 represents the fibration up to admissible coordinate changes and base automorphisms.

items.name: Nonrational fibers of zero-j models
items.statement: All fibers at nonrational base points in the three models of Theorem 10.5 are smooth.

items.name: Elliptic configurations on constant-Picard Enriques surfaces
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For an elliptic fibration, up to base automorphism the rational-fiber types are exactly among II*+E₄+I₁; II*+E₂+nonsplit I₁; III*+E₄+I₂; III*+E₂+nonsplit I₂; III*+E₄+E₄; IV*+E₃+IV; IV*+E₅+III; I₄*+E₄+E₂; I₁*+E₅+IV; I₁*+E₄+I₄; III+E₄+I₈.
items.note: Necessary possibilities, not assertions that all are realized by Enriques surfaces; the paper ultimately excludes the nonexceptional surfaces.

items.name: Quasielliptic configurations
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For a quasielliptic fibration, the three rational fibers have types among II*+II+II; III*+III+II; I₄*+II+II; I₂*+III+III, up to base automorphism.

items.name: Quasielliptic component sum
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For a quasielliptic fibration, r₀+r₁+r_∞=11. Its possible fiber symbols are II,III,I₂*,III*,II*,I₄*, with respective component counts 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 9.
items.note: The generic degree-zero Picard group is killed by 2; imports the quasielliptic classification, not yet fully source-extracted.

items.name: Forced multiple fibers
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. Every IV, IV*, II*, or I₁* fiber of a genus-one fibration is multiple.

items.name: Simple III* preliminary restriction
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. If a genus-one fibration has a simple III* fiber, it is elliptic and its rational-fiber configuration is III*+E₄+E₄.

items.name: Excluded rational two-section for exceptional-type half-fibers
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For a multiple fiber of type IV*, III*, or II*, there is no (-2)-curve R with R·F_ind=1.

items.name: Elimination of I₈
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has an I₈ fiber.

items.name: Elimination of II*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type II*.

items.name: Elimination of IV*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type IV*.

items.name: Elimination of IV
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type IV.

items.name: No multiple I₄*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a multiple I₄* fiber.

items.name: Eight residual configurations
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. Any genus-one fibration has, up to base automorphism, one of these rational-fiber configurations: elliptic I₄*+E₄+E₂, III*+E₄+I₂, III*+E₂+nonsplit I₂, III*+E₄+E₄, I₁*+E₄+I₄; quasielliptic I₄*+II+II, III*+III+II, I₂*+III+III.

items.name: Multiplicity restrictions in the residual table
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For any genus-one fibration, every I₁* fiber is multiple; fibers of type I₄*, I_n, and nonsplit I₂ are simple.

items.name: Partner fibration over F₂
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For every genus-one fibration ϕ there is ψ:Y→P¹ over F₂ with intersection ϕ⁻¹(∞)·ψ⁻¹(∞)=4.

items.name: Elimination of I₄*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type I₄*.

items.name: Six I₄* half-fiber incidence cases
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. If a simple I₄* fiber has components C₀,C₁ meeting C₂, chain C₂—C₃—C₄—C₅—C₆, and C₇,C₈ meeting C₆, then a half-fiber F of a partner fibration with F·(I₄* fiber)=2 has, up to graph symmetry, one of: F·C₂=1; F·C₃=1; F·C₄=1; F·C₀=F·C₁=1; F·C₀=F·C₈=1; F·C₀=2; unspecified intersections are 0.
items.note: The report’s exact orbit check enumerates 15 nonnegative incidence vectors of weighted degree 2 and obtains precisely the six listed graph-symmetry orbits. It does not prove realization or exclusion of those cases.

items.name: First forbidden ten-curve configuration
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. There is no simple-normal-crossing configuration of ten (-2)-curves C₀,…,C₈,R with affine D₈ graph C₀,C₁—C₂—C₃—C₄—C₅—C₆—C₇,C₈ and with R meeting only C₄ once.
items.note: The comma notation denotes forks at C₂ and C₆, not edges C₀—C₁ or C₇—C₈.

items.name: First ten-curve lattice discriminant
items.statement: In the hypothetical configuration of Proposition 12.2, S=⟨C₁,…,C₈,R,F⟩, with F a half-fiber of the I₄* fibration, has determinant−4 and index 2 in Num(Y); S*/S≅(Z/2)². The vector class represented by C₁* has norm−1 mod 2Z, and the two spinor classes C₇*,C₈* have norm−2 mod 2Z.
items.note: Full-norm mod 2Z is the paper convention. Built Tau Ceti uses half-norm modZ; translate, do not redefine the discriminant API.

items.name: Two-section of square zero or minus two
items.statement: In the lattice argument of Proposition 12.2, the nontrivial generic Picard quotient supplies an integral two-section R̃ with R̃²∈{0,−2}; the proof must apply the Enriques Reducibility Theorem, not assume R̃ is a rational curve.

items.name: Square-zero two-section calculation
items.statement: In the square-zero branch of Proposition 12.2, after choosing the spinor lift, the two-section class is C₈*+nR*+F* with n≥0, and its square is 2n; hence n=0.
acceptance: Compute with the inverse of matrix(14); preserve the zero-square branch.

items.name: Second forbidden ten-curve configuration
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. There is no configuration of ten (-2)-curves C₀,…,C₈,R whose C_i have affine D₈ incidence as above and with R·C₀=2, R·C₂=1, R·C_i=0 for other i. Require simple normal crossings away from the pair R,C₀.
items.note: Do not impose simple normal crossings on the pair R,C₀: the intersection number is 2.

items.name: Second ten-curve lattice discriminant
items.statement: For Proposition 12.3, the lattice S=⟨C₁,…,C₈,F′,F⟩ has Gram matrix D₈(-1)⊕U, determinant−4 and index 2 in Num(Y); its discriminant has two nonzero isotropic spinor classes and a vector class of odd full norm.

items.name: Generic degree-zero Picard quotient
items.statement: In Proposition 12.3, the quotient by vertical classes and the chosen degree-two class identifies the generic degree-zero Picard group, not the full Picard group of the generic genus-one curve.
items.note: The source displays Pic(Y_K); degree classes in 2Z are removed, so Pic⁰(Y_K) is the appropriate target.

items.name: Elimination of multiple III*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a multiple III* fiber.

items.name: Elimination of simple III*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a simple III* fiber.

items.name: Four simple III* half-fiber cases
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For the simple III* component numbering of §13, a half-fiber F of a partner fibration has, up to symmetry, incidences F·C₂=1; or F·C₀=F·C₇=1; or F·C₁=1; or F·C₀=2, with all other intersections 0.
items.note: The report’s exact orbit check enumerates 6 nonnegative incidence vectors of weighted degree 2 and obtains precisely the four listed graph-symmetry orbits. The geometric contradiction within each branch still imports the source prerequisites.

items.name: Final two-configuration impossibility
items.statement: Over any algebraically closed field, no classical Enriques surface has the configuration of reducible fibers of every genus-one fibration restricted to one of: I₁*+I₄ with the I₁* fiber multiple, or I₂*+III+III with two multiple fibers.
items.note: This last combinatorial theorem is not restricted to F₂. It first excludes I₁*, then multiple I₂*, then forces an excluded I₄ configuration.

items.name: No nonexceptional constant-Picard Enriques surface over F₂
items.statement: There is no Enriques surface over F₂ which is both nonexceptional and has constant full Picard scheme.

items.name: Low-degree off-diagonal Hodge vanishing
items.statement: If X/Q is proper smooth and, for every prime p, X acquires a smooth proper model over W(F_pbar), then H^j(X,Ω_X^i)=0 whenever i≠j and i+j≤3.
items.locator: §5, p. 16; Fontaine 1993 Theorem 1 and following remark(a)
items.note: The unramified Witt-ring version is essential; a theorem only for globally smooth proper Z-models is too weak for the stated application. Fontaine's theorem statement and remark were read visually, not its full proof.

items.name: No everywhere-unramified-good K3 surface
items.statement: No K3 surface X/Q has good reduction over W(F_pbar) for every prime p: the preceding theorem would give h^{2,0}=0, but a K3 surface has h^{2,0}=1.

items.name: Characteristic-two Enriques lifting criterion
items.statement: For an Enriques surface Y over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 2, Y is exceptional or supersingular iff it has no flat proper lift to W₂(k).
items.locator: Schröer 2021 Theorem 7.2, author pp. 23–24; main paper Theorem 5.2

items.name: Miniversal Enriques deformation ring
items.statement: For such Y, its miniversal complete local deformation ring A is regular and W(k)-flat with dimension 11 or 12. Dimension 12, absolute ramification index at least 2, exceptionality-or-supersingularity, and nonexistence of a W₂ lift are equivalent.
items.note: Proof reads §6 criterion and prior deformation theorem; full prerequisite closure still outstanding.

items.name: Dual lattice is the span of the dual basis
items.statement: For a nondegenerate integral lattice L and finite Z-basis b, its dual carrier is the Z-span of the bilinear-dual basis of the corresponding Q-basis.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Perfect lattice dual pairing
items.statement: For a nondegenerate integral lattice L, pairing gives a Z-linear equivalence L*≃Hom_Z(L,Z).
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Discriminant group representative equality
items.statement: For an integral lattice L and x,y∈L*, [x]=[y] in L*/L iff x−y∈L; in particular [x]=0 iff x∈L.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Finiteness of the discriminant group
items.statement: The quotient L*/L of an integral lattice is finite iff its rational form is nondegenerate.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Half-norm discriminant quadratic map
items.statement: For an even integral lattice L, the discriminant quadratic map on [x] equals B(x,x)/2 mod Z. Its value vanishes iff B(x,x) is twice an integer.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Polarization of the discriminant quadratic map
items.statement: For an even integral lattice, q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y) is the discriminant bilinear pairing of x,y.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Even overlattice correspondence
items.statement: For an even integral lattice L, even intermediate carriers L⊂M⊂L* are order-isomorphic to quadratic-isotropic subgroups of its discriminant quadratic module.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Overlattice index equals subgroup order
items.statement: For an integral lattice L and intermediate carrier M, [M:L] equals the cardinality of its associated subgroup in L*/L.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Signed determinant and index square
items.statement: For an integral intermediate carrier M which is a full lattice, det(M)[M:L]²=det(L).
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Discriminant and index square
items.statement: For an integral full intermediate lattice M, disc(M)[M:L]²=disc(L), using nonnegative discriminants.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Even D_n discriminant quadratic module
items.statement: For a positive even n, the positive-definite checkerboard D_n lattice has discriminant module (Z/2)² with vector half-norm 1/2, spinor and cospinor half-norm n/8, and vector-spinor pairing 1/2 mod Z.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: E₈ is even unimodular
items.statement: The standard positive E₈ root lattice is even and unimodular, with determinant 1.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: E₈ as the D₈-plus lattice
items.statement: The standard E₈ root lattice is isometric to the even index-two spinor extension D₈⁺.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization.

items.name: Surface Riemann–Roch
items.statement: For a smooth projective surface S over a field and divisor D, χ(O_S(D))=χ(O_S)+(D·(D−K_S))/2.
items.locator: §§4, 12; used to produce effective two-section classes
items.note: Reviewed SF.5 audit and full source contract read; the surface theorem is planned, not inferred from existing abstract quadratic forms.

items.name: Adjunction on a smooth surface
items.statement: For an integral Cartier curve C on a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field, 2p_a(C)−2=C·(C+K_S).
items.locator: §§4, 6, 12; use over an algebraically closed field for the displayed numerical formula
items.note: Reviewed SF.5 audit and full source contract read; the surface theorem is planned, not inferred from existing abstract quadratic forms.

items.name: Hodge index for a surface
items.statement: For a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field and ample divisor H, the intersection form is negative definite on the H-orthogonal subspace of NS(S)⊗R.
items.note: Reviewed SF.5 audit and full source contract read; the surface theorem is planned, not inferred from existing abstract quadratic forms.

items.name: Multiplicity and indecomposable fiber
items.statement: For a connected fiber-type effective divisor C=Σm_iC_i, its multiplicity is gcd_i m_i; C is simple if this is 1, multiple otherwise, and C_ind=Σ(m_i/m)C_i. Its reduction is ΣC_i, a different operation.

tests.name: MultiplicityandindecomposablefiberTest1
tests.statement: An I₄* fiber can be simple although some component coefficients are 2.

tests.name: MultiplicityandindecomposablefiberTest2
tests.statement: Multiplying a fiber divisor by 2 doubles its multiplicity.

tests.name: MultiplicityandindecomposablefiberTest3
tests.statement: A simple nonreduced fiber need not equal its reduction.

items.name: Semistable and unstable Kodaira symbols
items.statement: For a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, classify the underlying indecomposable geometric fiber: I_m with m≥1 is semistable/multiplicative; I_n* (n≥0),II,III,IV,IV*,III*,II* are unstable/additive; I₀ means a smooth elliptic underlying fiber.

tests.name: SemistableandunstableKodairasymbolsTest1
tests.statement: I₁ is semistable although its curve is irreducible.

tests.name: SemistableandunstableKodairasymbolsTest2
tests.statement: A smooth supersingular I₀ fiber is not additive.

tests.name: SemistableandunstableKodairasymbolsTest3
tests.statement: I₀* and I₀ have different component counts and reduction type.

items.name: Degenerate genus-one fiber
items.statement: A geometric fiber is degenerate when its underlying indecomposable curve is singular for an elliptic fibration, reducible for a quasielliptic fibration, or the fiber is multiple.

tests.name: DegenerategenusonefiberTest1
tests.statement: A multiple smooth elliptic fiber is degenerate.

tests.name: DegenerategenusonefiberTest2
tests.statement: A simple irreducible cuspidal fiber is the general quasielliptic fiber and is not degenerate in this convention.

tests.name: DegenerategenusonefiberTest3
tests.statement: Testing only geometric singularity misclassifies general quasielliptic fibers.

items.name: Nonsplit nodal conductor gluing
items.statement: Over a perfect field k, a rational nodal curve with nonsplit node is obtained by pinching Spec E⊂P¹_k, for a separable quadratic extension E/k, to Spec k; this is the symbol nonsplit I₁.

tests.name: NonsplitnodalconductorgluingTest1
tests.statement: Over F_q the count is q+2.

tests.name: NonsplitnodalconductorgluingTest2
tests.statement: Split I₁ instead identifies two rational points and has q points.

tests.name: NonsplitnodalconductorgluingTest3
tests.statement: A nonsplit node is not a cusp: its conductor algebra is a field, not k[ε]/ε².

items.name: Nonsplit two-component conductor gluing
items.statement: Over a perfect field k, nonsplit I₂ is the curve with normalization P¹⊔P¹ obtained from the conductor square Spec(E×E)→P¹⊔P¹ and Spec E→C, where E/k is separable quadratic.

tests.name: NonsplittwocomponentconductorgluingTest1
tests.statement: Over F_q it has 2q+2 points.

tests.name: NonsplittwocomponentconductorgluingTest2
tests.statement: Its two components are defined over k although their intersection points need not be.

tests.name: NonsplittwocomponentconductorgluingTest3
tests.statement: A split component graph does not force the two nodes to be k-rational.

items.name: Strong p-adic Hensel lemma
items.statement: Let p be prime, R a commutative semiring with an algebra map to Z_p, F∈R[X], and a∈Z_p. If ||F(a)||<||F′(a)||², there is a root z with ||z−a||<||F′(a)|| and ||F′(z)||=||F′(a)||, unique among roots satisfying that strict distance bound.
items.note: Actual generic coefficient hypotheses and full conclusion read at the pinned Mathlib commit. This does not by itself construct geometric sections of an algebraic space.

items.name: Dyadic unit square criterion
items.statement: For u∈Z₂×, u is a square in Q₂ iff u≡1 mod 8.
items.locator: Conrad Hensel’s Lemma, Theorem 4.5 and proof, p. 7; supplementary input to Proposition 5.5 repair
items.note: The layer explicitly plans U(Q₂,3)⊂squares and the sharpness witness 5. Necessity is reduction of an odd square modulo 8. Reviewed AUDIT-04 says the dyadic result is absent; do not cite the prime-to-residue-characteristic power-subgroup API at p=2.

items.name: Eight dyadic square classes in normal form
items.statement: Each c∈Q₂× has a unique square class represented by (−1)^e 2^a 5^b, with e,a,b∈{0,1}.
items.locator: Conrad Theorems 3.2, 4.5; elementary deduction in this continuation’s cover-comparison proof
items.note: Application of the existing layer’s multiplicative-group, dyadic eight-class and deep-unit contracts: valuation parity and odd residue modulo 8 give the explicit basis. This basis computation is an application, not a second local-field roadmap.

items.name: Unramified quadratic correction torsor
items.statement: The Z₂-algebra B=Z₂[z]/(z²−z−1), with involution z↦1−z, defines a finite étale Z/2-torsor. Its generic fiber is Q₂(√5), and its special fiber is F₄.
items.locator: Supplementary dyadic model in the Proposition 5.5 repair; LocalFieldsRamification Layer 2 worked Q₂(√5) example
items.note: Discriminant 5 is a unit; modulo 2 the polynomial is irreducible and separable. The involution exchanges its roots. This gives an actual integral model; Z₂[s]/(s²−5) is not an étale model.
api: finite-étale torsor identity and residue extension

tests.name: SCH23_175_1
tests.statement: Modulo 2 neither 0 nor 1 is a root, and the derivative is 1.

tests.name: SCH23_175_2
tests.statement: (2z−1)²=5; base change to W(F₂bar) splits the torsor.

tests.name: SCH23_175_3
tests.statement: The polynomial s²−5 has derivative 2s and does not present an étale Z₂-algebra.

items.name: Canonical-cover twists supported at two
items.statement: Let S=Spec Z[1/2], Y/S an Enriques family with Pic^τ=μ₂, and X→Y a canonical Z/2-cover. For u∈{1,−1,2,−2}, the contracted product X^(u)=(X×_S Spec O_S[s]/(s²−u))/(Z/2) is a canonical finite étale double cover of Y.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4 twisting action; explicit construction supplementing Proposition 5.5
api: compatibility with pullback and composition of twists
preservation of the edge-map canonical-cover class

tests.name: SCH23_176_1
tests.statement: u=1 yields the original cover up to isomorphism.

tests.name: SCH23_176_2
tests.statement: Twisting successively by u and v agrees with the uv square class.

tests.name: SCH23_176_3
tests.statement: Using u=5 over Z[1/2] introduces ramification at 5; it is not one of these globally allowed corrections.

items.name: Canonical cover over Z₂ before Picard constancy
items.statement: If Y/Z is an Enriques family with Pic^τ=μ₂, its restriction to Z₂ has a canonical finite étale double cover X₂→Y_Z₂.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5 repair, step 1; Corollary 7.3 and Proposition 5.4(ii)
items.note: Minkowski first makes Num constant. Corollary 7.3 uses Num only and gives 25 points on Y_F₂. Smooth henselian lifting gives Y(Z₂)≠∅, so Proposition 5.4(ii) applies. Neither full Picard constancy nor Theorem 15.1 is used.

items.name: Dyadic difference class of canonical covers
items.statement: For two canonical Z/2-covers of the same Enriques surface over Q₂, their difference under the twisting action is a class in H¹(Q₂,Z/2)=Q₂×/Q₂×². In particular this applies to a cover over Z[1/2] and the generic fiber of the cover in /177.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4 final assertion; repair of Proposition 5.5
items.note: Identify Z/2 with μ₂ only over Q₂, where 2 is invertible. Kummer over Z₂ classifies μ₂-torsors, not all finite étale Z/2-torsors.

items.name: Removing the ramified part of the difference
items.statement: Let c∈Q₂×/Q₂×² be a difference class as in /178. Exactly one u∈{1,−1,2,−2} has cu∈{1,5}. Twisting the global cover by u and the Z₂-cover by the trivial torsor or /175, respectively, makes their Q₂-fibers isomorphic.
items.locator: This continuation’s proof of the previously unverified Proposition 5.5 comparison
items.note: If c=(−1)^e2^a5^b, choose u=(−1)^e2^a. Each class has exponent 2, so cu=5^b. The remaining class already has a finite étale Z₂-model; no approximation over Frac W(F₂bar) is asserted.

items.name: Everywhere unramified number fields have degree one
items.statement: For a number field F, if each nonzero prime ideal q of its ring of integers has ramification index 1 over Z, then [F:Q]=1.
items.locator: TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Inertia.lean:89; arithmetic input used on main-paper p. 15
items.note: Actual statement and hypotheses read at f790474. The scheme-theoretic finite-étale translation remains a separate item /181.

items.name: The étale fundamental group of Spec Z is trivial
items.statement: Every connected nonempty finite étale cover of Spec Z is isomorphic to Spec Z; consequently π₁(Spec Z)=1 and every finite-rank locally constant free abelian sheaf on Spec Z is constant.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5 first paragraph; deduction from /180 and the finite-étale Galois category
items.note: A connected finite étale Z-algebra is a normal domain, hence the full ring of integers of its fraction number field; its ramification indices are 1. Import /180. This is not already the statement of the number-field declaration.

items.name: Picard classes are represented when a section exists
items.statement: Let f:X→B be a morphism of algebraic spaces with a section σ and universally O_T≅f_{T,*}O_{X_T}. For every B-scheme T, the sequence 0→Pic(T)→Pic(X_T)→Pic_{X/B}(T)→0 is split exact, with retraction σ_T*.
items.locator: Stacks Lemma 99.11.4, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24; local-projectivity supplement to Proposition 5.5
items.note: Statement and descent proof read. The section rigidifies descent isomorphisms; no vanishing of Br(B) is needed.

items.name: Lifting twice a numerical class
items.statement: For an exact sequence 0→P→Q→N→0 of abelian fppf sheaves with 2P=0, multiplication by 2 on Q descends uniquely to a map d:N→Q, with projection∘d=[2]_N. Apply this to Pic^τ→Pic→Num of an Enriques family in the Pic^τ=μ₂ branch.
items.locator: Elementary sheaf descent supplement to Proposition 5.5, using its exact sequence(3)
api: unique factorization through the sheaf quotient

tests.name: SCH23_183_1
tests.statement: For a split extension P⊕N, d(n)=(0,2n).

tests.name: SCH23_183_2
tests.statement: Two local lifts differ by P and therefore have the same double.

tests.name: SCH23_183_3
tests.statement: d is not a splitting of Q→N: its composite is multiplication by 2, not the identity.

items.name: Local projectivity for the excluded μ₂ branch
items.statement: Let R be a noetherian local ring and Y/R an Enriques family with a section, constant Num, and Pic^τ annihilated by 2. Then Y is a projective R-scheme. In particular an Enriques family over Z in the Pic^τ=μ₂ branch becomes projective over Z_p for every prime p.
items.locator: This continuation’s local-model supplement to Proposition 5.5
items.note: Lift the numerical class of an ample line bundle on the closed fiber to constant Num(R); /183 and /182 give a line bundle with twice that numerical class. Ampleness on the projective closed surface is invariant under numerical equivalence. /186 spreads ampleness over the local base, so Y is a scheme and projective. For R=Z_p, /79 gives 1+10p+p² rational points; /185 supplies the section. No claim that an arbitrary proper algebraic space is projective.

items.name: Smooth henselian lifting for the local family
items.statement: Let R be a henselian local ring with residue field k, and X/R a smooth separated algebraic space. Every k-point lifts to an R-point.
items.locator: Stacks Lemma 68.11.4 at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EMV and Lemma 15.13.3 at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H74
items.note: A separated space is decent. Choose an affine étale neighborhood with the same residue field at the given point, then apply smooth-algebra lifting for (R,m). Statements and proofs read; this avoids presuming X was a scheme.

items.name: Spreading a fiberwise ample line bundle
items.statement: Let f:X→B be a proper algebraic space over a noetherian scheme and L an invertible sheaf. If X_b is a scheme and L_b is ample, some open neighborhood V of b makes X_V a scheme with L_V relatively ample.
items.note: Import the existing relative-ampleness and algebraic-space-descent owners. Read the proof constructing a finite morphism to projective space; ampleness is an essential hypothesis, not a consequence of properness alone.

items.name: Finite étale twisting preserves good models
items.statement: Let R be a ring, Y/R smooth proper, G/R finite étale, X→Y a finite étale G-torsor, and T/R a G-torsor, with G commutative. The contracted product X×^G T remains finite étale over Y and smooth proper over R. If Y is projective over R, the contracted product is a projective R-scheme.
items.locator: Effective descent applied to Proposition 5.4 twists; finite étale descent and pullback of an ample line bundle
items.note: Descend the finite étale morphism to Y, then pull back Y’s ample line bundle. This is not a claim that arbitrary unpolarized projective varieties descend as projective schemes.

items.name: Étale canonical covers are K3 surfaces
items.statement: For an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field whose canonical-cover Cartier dual G is étale of rank 2, its canonical G-torsor is a smooth connected K3 surface. This includes ordinary Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2 and all Enriques surfaces in characteristic different from 2.
items.locator: Main-paper §4 and Proposition 5.5; canonical-cover theorem from the Enriques prerequisites
items.note: Distinct from /40–/41, which concern the singular K3-like covers in the simply connected characteristic-two cases. The geometric K3 theorem is imported; the original Enriques prerequisite proof remains in the recursive-source gap.

items.name: Kodaira–Néron classification of fibers of genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over an algebraically closed field. For every closed point b the underlying indecomposable curve of canonical type f⁻¹_ind(b)=Σn_iC_i is one of: I₀ (a smooth genus-one curve); I₁ (a rational nodal curve); I_m, m≥2 (a cycle of m smooth rational (−2)-curves, all n_i=1); II (a rational cuspidal curve); III (two smooth rational curves meeting in one point with multiplicity 2); IV (three smooth rational curves through one point); I_n*, n≥0 (n+5 components, dual graph the extended Dynkin diagram D̃_{n+4}); IV*, III*, II* (7, 8, 9 components, dual graphs Ẽ₆, Ẽ₇, Ẽ₈), the n_i being the coefficients of the null root. The components of a reducible fiber are (−2)-curves, and its intersection matrix is negative semidefinite with radical generated by f⁻¹_ind(b).
items.note: Néron 1964 and Kodaira 1963; valid in every characteristic, and for quasi-elliptic fibrations (characteristic 2 and 3) the reducible fibers are of additive type. Items /167–/171 define the symbols and their twisted forms; this is the classification theorem they presuppose. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 plans the equation-level Kodaira types over a DVR, not fibers of fibered surfaces.

items.name: Kodaira symbols for schematic fibers over non-closed fields (Szydło)
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over a field and a∈B a closed point. If every irreducible component of the schematic fiber S_a is birational to P¹ over κ(a), then Γ(S_ā)→Γ(S_a) is a graph isomorphism respecting edge labels and the Kodaira symbol of the geometric fiber describes f⁻¹_ind(a). With at most two components the twisted forms Ĩ₁, ĨI, Ĩ₂, ĨII of /170–/171 also occur; over a perfect residue field only Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂ do.
items.note: Szydło, Elliptic fibers over non-perfect residue fields, J. Number Theory 104 (2004), 75–99; stated as the paper uses it.

items.name: Canonical bundle formula for genus-one fibrations (Bombieri–Mumford)
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over an algebraically closed field, with multiple fibers m_iF_i. Write R¹f_*O_S=L⊕T with L invertible and T torsion. Then ω_S≅f*(ω_B⊗L^{−1})⊗O_S(Σa_iF_i) with 0≤a_i≤m_i−1, a_i=m_i−1 for every tame multiple fiber, and deg L^{−1}=χ(O_S)+length(T).
items.note: Bombieri–Mumford, Enriques' classification of surfaces in char. p, II (1977), Theorem 2. Used for ω_J=φ*O(d) in /72 and for ω_Y≅O_Y(F₁−F₂) in /35.

items.name: Tame and wild multiple fibers
items.statement: Let mF (m≥2, F the underlying indecomposable curve) be a multiple fiber of a genus-one fibration f:S→B over an algebraically closed field. The line bundle O_F(F) has finite order ν dividing m; the fiber is tame if ν=m and wild otherwise, and it is wild exactly when the torsion of R¹f_*O_S is supported at its image point. On an Enriques surface with H¹(Y,O_Y)=0 every multiple fiber is tame, so each double fiber 2F has O_F(F) of order 2 in Pic(F).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 12; proof of Theorem 5.6(iv), p. 17
items.note: Raynaud; Bombieri–Mumford II, §2; Katsura–Ueno. Lemma 4.3 (/36) and Theorem 5.6(iv) (/69) consume it.

items.name: Lang's theorem for genus-one curves over finite fields
items.statement: Every torsor under a connected algebraic group over a finite field is trivial (Lang 1956, Theorem 2). In particular every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus one over F_q has an F_q-point and is an elliptic curve.
items.locator: §3 before Proposition 3.3, p. 11; proof of Proposition 9.2, p. 24
items.note: Not planned in the atlas: no layer treats Galois cohomology of connected algebraic groups over finite fields. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3 counts points of elliptic curves, not of torsors.

items.name: Twisted forms of P¹ over finite fields
items.statement: A proper curve C over F_q with C⊗F̄_q≅P¹ is isomorphic to P¹_{F_q}, because Br(F_q)=0 by Wedderburn's little theorem. Over any field, a twisted form of P¹ that carries a line bundle of degree one is isomorphic to P¹.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 11; proof of Theorem 5.6(iii), p. 17
items.note: Mathlib has Wedderburn's little theorem (Mathlib/RingTheory/LittleWedderburn.lean:166, littleWedderburn); Brauer–Severi curves and the Brauer group of a field are not in the libraries at the pins.

items.name: Isogenous elliptic curves over a finite field have the same point counts
items.statement: If elliptic curves E and E′ over F_q are isogenous over F_q, then #E(F_{q^r})=#E′(F_{q^r}) for every r≥1. This is the direction of Tate's isogeny theorem (Tate 1966, Theorem 1) that the paper uses.
items.note: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layers 1 and 3 plan isogenies commuting with Frobenius and #E(F_q)=deg(1−π_q); the invariance of the counts under isogeny is not stated there. FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4 plans the isogeny theorem over number fields.

items.name: Invariants of rational elliptic surfaces
items.statement: Let φ:J→P¹ be a relatively minimal elliptic fibration with a section E of a smooth projective rational surface over an algebraically closed field. Then ω_J≅φ*O_{P¹}(−1), K_J²=0 and (E·E)=−1, and J is obtained from P² by nine blowing-ups; hence b₂(J)=ρ(J)=10 and Num(J) is odd unimodular of signature (1,9).
items.locator: proof of Proposition 6.1, p. 18; proof of Corollary 7.3, p. 21; proof of Proposition 9.5, p. 27
items.note: Cossec–Dolgachev 1989, Proposition 5.6.1. /72 records the consequences for the Weierstrass model.

items.name: Quasi-elliptic fibrations in characteristic two
items.statement: Quasi-elliptic fibrations exist only in characteristics 2 and 3. For a quasi-elliptic fibration φ:S→P¹ of a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, every fiber is irreducible cuspidal (type II) or reducible of type III, I*_{2n}, III* or II* (with 2, 2n+5, 8 and 9 components), and the Mordell–Weil group of the jacobian is killed by 2. Hence ρ(S)=2+Σ_b(r_b−1), r_b the number of components of the fiber over b; for ρ(S)=10 this gives Σ_b(r_b−1)=8.
items.note: Cossec–Dolgachev 1989, Theorems 5.7.4–5.7.6. /120 and /121 consume it.

items.name: Lang's classification of rational elliptic surfaces in characteristic two (as used)
items.statement: (Lang 2000) Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2 the configurations of singular fibers of relatively minimal rational jacobian elliptic surfaces are classified, with normal forms of their Weierstrass equations y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆ (deg a_i≤i).
